analysis.title: 1% Of Companies Account For 80% Of OpenAI And Anthropic Spending - And It Just Stalled
key_insights: Ramp, tracking payments across 70,000+ US businesses, reports the top 1% of companies account for 80% of business spending on OpenAI and Anthropic, more concentrated than any other software category it tracks.
Median VC-backed startup spent $76 per employee per month on AI, more than ten times the $7 at private equity-backed firms (Ramp summer report).
YipitData: Anthropic's top 1% of customers generated 46% of its revenue in August, up from 25% a year earlier.

Anthropic's IPO prospectus shows two unnamed customers generated nearly a quarter of its 2025 revenue (Reuters). Cursor and GitHub Copilot reportedly drove about $1.2B of Anthropic's $5B annualized run-rate last year (VentureBeat).

The article describes a circular funding loop: Coatue invested in both Cursor's parent Anysphere and Anthropic's $30B Series G, Cursor spends on Claude tokens, and that revenue supports the valuation of Coatue's Anthropic stake. Ramp itself raised $1.85B at a $60B valuation, with investors that also backed Anthropic's Series G.
Ramp's October AI Index: top 1% of AI-spending firms spent $9,568 per employee in September, up 11.7% from August but 3.1% below July's peak of $9,873.

Ramp recorded two straight months (August and September) of virtually no growth in token spend while raw token volumes kept rising. Total dollar spend set a new high in early October, only 1.5% above the August peak.

Ramp economist Kharazian attributes the stall to falling prices at the frontier plus efficiency and quality gains lowering the blended price per million tokens. Enterprise contracts include discounts from sticker price, so they could cut prices without adding volume.

Paid AI adoption across Ramp's network rose only 0.62 points to 55.9% in September. Kharazian says the market looks to be at the top of the S-curve, with growth needing to come from more intense adoption rather than more customers.

Ornn Anthropic Token Price Index fell to $0.83 per million tokens from above $1.70 in mid-September, a record low since the June launch. OpenAI's index is $0.45, after it cut GPT-5.6 Luna and Terra rates by up to 80% in late July, three days after Moonshot released Kimi K3 open weights. OpenAI has reportedly leaned toward delaying its IPO to 2027.

Goldman (Sept. 25 note): token demand growth must outpace falling token prices to support investment spending. Total token demand is up about 18-fold since December, while demand for high-margin frontier models has grown only half as fast.
Goldman estimates realized ROIC across Amazon, Alphabet, Meta, Microsoft and Oracle fell from 40% to 25%, the lowest in its data back to 2016.

Apollo's Torsten Slok, citing Ramp, argues compute demand is flat and highly price-sensitive, so buyers throttle usage or switch to cheap open-source models when prices move. He says the price users will pay is the key variable for data center construction economics.
Citadel's Ken Griffin told Bloomberg markets are almost certainly in an AI bubble.

sector_views.rationale: Falling realized token prices and flat dollar spend squeeze returns on data center investment. Goldman puts hyperscaler ROIC at 25%, down from 40%.

risk_factors: Dollar spend on frontier AI models is flat while token volumes rise, because realized prices are falling.
Revenue concentration: top 1% of customers drive 80% of spend at OpenAI and Anthropic combined, and 46% of Anthropic revenue.
Customers hold leverage in enterprise contracts, and discounts cut prices without adding volume.
Open-source substitution (Kimi K3) is pressuring frontier model pricing and demand.
Hyperscaler ROIC is declining, which threatens the case for continued data center capex.
Circular funding among AI investors and customers may inflate reported revenue and valuations.
cross_bank_references: Goldman Sachs Sept. 25 note: token demand growth will need to outpace declining token prices to support continued growth in investment spending.
Apollo's Slok citing Ramp: compute demand is flat and highly price-sensitive.

tension_points.bull_case: Jevons paradox: cheaper tokens drive usage high enough to raise total revenue. Token volumes are up about 18-fold since December.
tension_points.bear_case: Dollar spend is flat despite rising volumes. Frontier model demand is growing at half the rate of total demand, and buyers are price-sensitive and substitute cheap open-source models.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Goldman: token demand growth must outpace declining token prices. Renewed growth in dollar token spend per Ramp would undercut the bear case.

theme_stances.key_argument: Token volumes rise but dollar spend is flat because blended prices per token are falling.
theme_stances.evidence: two straight months of virtually no growth in token spend

theme_stances.key_argument: A small set of venture-backed customers drives most lab revenue, and many are funded by the labs' own investors.
theme_stances.evidence: Just 1% of companies account for 80% of all business spending
